summary: Feed s184_triple to IDS is degraded with 3 faults: VLAN 20 missing (high), high encrypted share above IDS tolerance (medium), and duplicate packets (medium). No packet drops, one-way, or overload detected.

findings.root_cause: Required VLAN 20 not seen and 50% of packets are untagged. Packet broker or SPAN trunk is stripping 802.1Q tags or not forwarding VLAN 20 to this IDS tool port, despite IDS requiring VLANs 10 and 20.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS has zero visibility into VLAN 20 segment; attacks or lateral movement on that VLAN will be missed, creating a major detection coverage gap.

recommended_fix.why: Restore and preserve 802.1Q tags for VLANs 10 and 20 through the broker to the IDS so policy and detection for VLAN 20 is restored.

findings.root_cause: 74% of bytes are encrypted, exceeding the IDS tolerance of 60%. Traffic is predominantly TLS/encrypted and is being forwarded without selective decryption or filtering at the packet broker.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires full payload inspection but is blind to most traffic; encrypted payloads cannot be inspected for exploits/malware, sharply reducing detection efficacy and wasting IDS cycles.

recommended_fix.why: IDS cannot detect threats inside encryption; decrypt relevant flows at broker/proxy or filter bulk encrypted traffic so IDS receives inspectable payload within its 60% tolerance.

findings.root_cause: 8.0% duplicates (221 of 2752 packets) indicates overlapping SPAN/mirror sources or dual TAP feeds aggregated without deduplication on the packet broker, sending the same packet twice to the IDS.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes CPU/storage re-analyzing identical packets, inflates event counts, can cause false correlation and masks true traffic rates; at 8% it exceeds 5% threshold.

recommended_fix.why: Enable broker deduplication to deliver only unique packets to the 1G IDS port, freeing capacity for real detection.
